LESSON: WRITING 13.5.1 CREATIVE WRITING: NARRATIVE COMPOSITION

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 13
Topic 13.5: Writing 13.5.1 Creative Writing: Narrative Composition

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 13.5.1 Creative Writing: Narrative Composition. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What makes a story memorable?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain the meaning of specified idioms in context
2. create well-written narrative compositions using the specified idioms
3. appreciate the role of idioms in creative writing

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WRITING 13.5.1 CREATIVE WRITING: NARRATIVE COMPOSITION
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Writing 13.5.1 Creative Writing: Narrative Composition helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WRITING 13.5.1 CREATIVE WRITING: NARRATIVE COMPOSITION
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Explain the meaning of specified idioms in context

What this means
In this part you learn to explain the meaning of specified idioms in context. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain the meaning of specified idioms in context.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 13.5.1 Creative Writing: Narrative Composition”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain the meaning of specified idioms in context. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Create well-written narrative compositions using the specified idioms

What this means
In this part you learn to create well-written narrative compositions using the specified idioms. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: create well-written narrative compositions using the specified idioms.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 13.5.1 Creative Writing: Narrative Composition to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can create well-written narrative compositions using the specified idioms. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the role of idioms in creative writing

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the role of idioms in creative writing. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the role of idioms in creative writing.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the role of idioms in creative writing. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Writing 13.5.1 Creative Writing: Narrative Composition is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 13.5.1 Creative Writing: Narrative Composition”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: explain the meaning of specified idioms in context)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 13.5.1 Creative Writing: Narrative Composition to a partner. (skill: create well-written narrative compositions using the specified idioms)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate the role of idioms in creative writing)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Writing 13.5.1 Creative Writing: Narrative Composition to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain the meaning of specified idioms in context.
3. Practise this skill: create well-written narrative compositions using the specified idioms.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the role of idioms in creative writing.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Writing 13.5.1 Creative Writing: Narrative Composition from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Writing 13.5.1 Creative Writing: Narrative Composition: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Writing 13.5.1 Creative Writing: Narrative Composition?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What makes a story memorable?
2. What is the importance of using idioms in communication?
3. How can we respond effectively to a road crash that occurs in our vicinity?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Writing 13.5.1 Creative Writing: Narrative Composition means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain the meaning of specified idioms in context.
5. Be able to: create well-written narrative compositions using the specified idioms.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
